jobs.description:
Vantive is a vital organ therapy company on a mission to extend lives and expand possibilities for patients and care teams everywhere. For 70 years, our team has driven meaningful innovations in kidney care. As we build on our legacy, we are deepening our commitment to elevating the dialysis experience through digital solutions and advanced services, while looking beyond kidney care and investing in transforming vital organ therapies. Greater flexibility and efficiency in therapy administration for care teams, and longer, fuller lives for patients— that is what Vantive aspires to deliver.

We believe Vantive will not only build our leadership in the kidney care space, it will also offer meaningful work to those who join us. At Vantive, you will become part of a community of people who are focused, courageous and don’t settle for the mediocre. Each of us is driven to help improve patients’ lives worldwide. Join us in advancing our mission to extend lives and expand possibilities.

As the Global Software Leader for Acute Products/ Devices, this role is responsible for leading multi-site device software engineering team for Acute Care products by defining and driving software strategy and implementation and delivering to all Acute Care product lines. As the Global Device Software Leader for Acute Care product lines of Vantive, works in collaboration with commercial, systems, program management, Quality & Regulatory functional leadership teams to build and execute on product strategy, roadmaps and delivery plans.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Own product-line software strategy and roadmaps for device software for all acute products; aligning with business and product strategy and therapy needs.
Lead Acute global device software team, including functional managers and technical leaders.
Lead defining and implementing technology and software architecture strategy working with Acute device software leaders and in collaboration with systems leaders
Lead Acute global device software team in building execution plans and driving execution to deliver to the product roadmaps and releases across all Acute product lines.
Create, effectively communicate, and realize vision and strategy for the organization that aligns with the business and customer needs.
Establish an organization structure that ensures clear accountability and operational excellence.
Develop and mentor high-performing managers and technical leaders; build succession plans and communities of practice across global sites.
Provide strategic planning leadership for resource staffing and project execution with proactive management of technical and project risk to ensure delivery of business commitments
Leverages deep knowledge of technology/process/therapy domains, user needs, hazards, risk, and business targets and budgets to drive solutions and product design realization.
Management of technical and project risk to ensure delivery of business commitments.
Drive post-market software change management strategy, field data analytics, and reliability improvements with contained risk and minimal therapy disruption.
Embrace and embed agile ways of working in support of a fail-fast-learn-fast culture and enabling continual improvement.
Foster a collaborative work environment with strong working relationships within and across businesses and functions, and with strategic external partners.
Maintain current knowledge of relevant Quality System Regulations and other regulatory requirements related to research and development (medical product development, design, safety, Cyber Security) to ensure compliance in all research, development, data collection and reporting activities.

Qualifications

Significant experience in Electro-mechanical devices and device software engineering.
Understanding of global regulatory requirements for medical devices; risk and reliability concepts for development; and the need to deliver quality products and/or processes.
Significant experience leading a globally distributed team and working in a global matrix environment.
Strong team building and talent management skills, and the ability to motivate team members to achieve goals.
Proven experience in driving product specific and overall portfolio strategy, specific to software technology, in a global business.
Must possess strong knowledge of scientific/technical disciplines and solid knowledge of related disciplines such as regulatory, quality, and/or product development.
Recognized internally and externally as expert in functional area.
Must be a strategic, innovative problem solver, and have strong influencing and communication skills.
Exceptional stakeholder management and communication skills across Clinical, RA/QA, Systems, Operations, and suppliers.

Education and/or Experience

Bachelor’s degree in electrical/computer/software engineering (Master’s preferred). Experience in medical devices or other safety‑critical electromechanical domains (e.g., aerospace, industrial controls, automotive) required; medical device experience strongly preferred.

About Midi Health:

Midi Health is transforming healthcare for women in midlife, delivering expert, personalized care through a virtual-first platform built around the needs of women in perimenopause and menopause.

We’re growing quickly, and technology is at the center of how we reach more patients, create an exceptional care experience, and scale access to high-quality care nationwide. We’re looking for leaders who are excited to build at that intersection of healthcare, technology, and consumer experience.

The Role:

We’re looking for a Director of Engineering, Growth & Consumer to lead the engineering teams behind Midi’s patient experience — from the moment someone first discovers Midi through registration, onboarding, booking, and ongoing engagement with their care.

This is a true player-coach role. You’ll lead and develop a high-performing engineering team while staying close to the technology: shaping architecture, reviewing code, using AI coding tools, and helping your team solve hard problems.

You’ll also be a senior engineering partner to Product, Marketing, Design, Data Science, and Clinical leaders. We expect our engineering leaders to think beyond their immediate teams, contribute to company-wide technical decisions, and help shape how we build as Midi scales.

Lead the engineering roadmap and execution for Midi’s consumer and growth experiences, including registration, onboarding, appointment booking, patient engagement, prescription and supplement commerce, and growth loops.
Build and lead high-performing engineering teams with a culture of ownership, accountability, speed, and high technical standards.
Stay hands-on with the technology through architecture decisions, code reviews, prototyping, and AI-assisted development.
Partner closely with Product, Marketing, Design, and Data Science to translate business and patient needs into scalable technical solutions.
Drive engineering quality, velocity, reliability, and operational health across your area.
Hire, mentor, and develop engineers and engineering leaders as the organization grows.

Help define how Midi uses AI and modern development tools to fundamentally improve how software is built.

What We’re Looking For:

Deep software engineering foundation. You’ve spent meaningful time as a senior individual contributor building sophisticated applications and consumer-facing experiences.
Proven engineering leadership. You have 5+ years of engineering management experience and have led organizations of 10+ engineers.
Player-coach mindset. You’re comfortable operating at the leadership level while remaining technically credible and close enough to the work to help your team make better decisions.
Strong product and consumer instincts. You understand that great engineering isn’t just about technical elegance — it’s about building experiences that drive meaningful outcomes for users and the business.
Executive-level communication and judgment. You can confidently partner with senior leaders, navigate ambiguity, influence direction, and communicate technical tradeoffs clearly.
Exceptional cross-functional instincts. You naturally build trust with Product, Design, Marketing, Data Science, and other non-engineering partners.
AI-native approach to engineering. You’ve recently built or shipped something meaningful using AI coding agents and have a practical understanding of how AI is changing what engineering teams can accomplish.

Strong ownership mindset. You close loops, take accountability for outcomes, and step into problems rather than waiting for someone else to solve them.

Nice to Have:

Experience leading Growth Engineering, Consumer Engineering, Martech, or digital commerce teams.
Experience building high-scale consumer products where conversion, engagement, retention, or experimentation are core to the business.
Experience with Python, Django, React, and AWS.
Experience working in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated environment.
Experience building experimentation platforms, personalization systems, or AI-powered consumer experiences.

Why Midi:

This is an opportunity to build technology that directly impacts how women access healthcare — at a company experiencing significant growth and still early enough that engineering leaders can have an outsized impact.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape not only the products patients use, but also how Midi’s engineering organization operates, scales, and takes advantage of a rapidly changing technology landscape.

If you’re energized by building consumer experiences, developing exceptional engineering teams, and rethinking what’s possible with AI-native software development, we’d love to hear from you.

The Rockefeller Center Operations (RCO) Facilities Engineering team manages all aspects of the Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Fire Alarm, Fire Protection (MEPFP), emergency power, BMS, mission-critical, and life-safety systems for the 24x7 operations in the NY, NJ, and Washington, DC campuses, encompassing approximately 2.5M square feet across 10 commercial buildings of production, technical, and office space.

The Sr. Director of Engineering

Ensure the integrity and operation of the facilities critical infrastructure systems which are paramount to our operational reliability, where the goal is a 99.999% on-air performance

Provide technical assistance and support to the Fire Life Safety team, with the operation, upgrade, and maintenance of the fire alarm systems throughout the facilities

The ability to develop and present presentation material in a concise and effective manner

Position Overview

We are seeking a Director, Gas Infrastructure to add pipeline-specific technical depth to Hanwha Energy USA's growing natural gas infrastructure and generation initiatives. The Director will serve as the company's lead technical resource for the evaluation and advancement of pipeline transportation, storage, compression, interconnection, and other gas infrastructure opportunities. The role will also support technical due diligence for gas-fired generation and related infrastructure investments.

The Director will lead technical workstreams from early screening through due diligence, investment approval, contracting support, and project handoff. Responsibilities include assessing physical feasibility, system operations, integrity and reliability, capital requirements, schedule considerations, and execution risks, and translating those findings into actionable recommendations for development, investment, and operational decision-making. For gas-fired acquisitions and investments, the Director will focus on fuel supply infrastructure, pipeline connectivity, and related technical considerations while coordinating broader plant evaluations with engineering and external subject matter experts.

This role serves as the company's primary technical authority for natural gas transportation and infrastructure matters. The position is responsible for evaluating infrastructure opportunities, identifying technical risks and constraints, supporting strategic planning efforts, and providing technical expertise throughout the project lifecycle. The role works closely with commercial, engineering, environmental, regulatory, and operational teams to ensure infrastructure decisions are grounded in sound technical analysis and aligned with business objectives. The employee may be required to perform other job-related duties as requested by management. All duties will be assigned in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

The employee may be required to perform other job-related duties as requested by management. All duties will be assigned in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

Responsibilities

Pipeline Infrastructure and System Operations

Evaluate interstate and intrastate transmission pipelines, gathering systems, storage facilities, compression, metering, regulation, dehydration, and receipt and delivery interconnections.
Assess pipeline hydraulics, pressure profiles, compression requirements, system bottlenecks, fuel use, redundancy, outage exposure, expansion capability, and practical gas deliverability under normal and peak conditions.
Review pipeline operating data, maintenance practices, control-room management, SCADA and telecommunications, cybersecurity interfaces, emergency response, operator qualification, and reliability risks.
Evaluate integrity-management programs, inline inspection and direct-assessment results, corrosion control, anomaly remediation, class location and high-consequence areas, maximum allowable operating pressure records, leak history, and remaining-life considerations.
Identify pipeline compliance, land, environmental, and permitting issues that may affect feasibility, cost, schedule, operation, expansion, or transfer, and coordinate detailed review with the Environmental Permitting Manager and legal counsel.

Commercial Support

Partner directly with the Director, Gas Origination to screen and evaluate pipeline, lateral, storage, compression, and interconnection opportunities, including greenfield projects, brownfield expansions, joint ventures, and anchor-shipper positions.
Develop technical scopes, data-room requests, site-visit plans, management questions, and advisor workplans aligned with commercial priorities and transaction schedules.
Test proposed capacity and deliverability against hydraulic studies, compressor availability, outage assumptions, receipt and delivery pressures, gas quality requirements, downstream constraints, tariff provisions, and operating requirements.
Review route, design basis, constructability, cost estimates, schedule, procurement strategy, commissioning plans, and cost-to-complete exposure for pipeline additions and expansions; provide inputs to the Environmental Permitting Manager for permit strategy and schedule.
Provide technical assumptions for commercial negotiations and investment models, including capacity, availability, fuel loss, operating cost, maintenance capital, expansion capital, schedule, and contingency.

Gas Asset Due Diligence

Support technical due diligence for acquisitions and investments involving simple-cycle and combined-cycle generation assets, with particular emphasis on fuel supply infrastructure, pipeline interfaces, pressure and gas-quality requirements, storage, firm transportation, and no-notice capability.
Evaluate operating performance and asset condition, including heat rate, capacity, starts, equivalent operating hours, forced outages, degradation, major maintenance intervals, long-term service agreements, spare-parts strategy, and near-term capital requirements.
Coordinate specialist review of gas turbines, steam turbines, heat recovery steam generators, generators, balance-of-plant systems, electrical systems, water systems, and emissions controls when broader plant expertise is required.
Identify environmental permit conditions, operating limits, compliance history, and monitoring obligations that affect asset capability or value, and coordinate detailed environmental review with the Environmental Permitting Manager.

Due Diligence and Investment Support

Lead or coordinate independent technical due diligence for pipeline and gas infrastructure acquisitions, equity investments, transportation commitments, and strategic partnerships.
Integrate engineering, operational, environmental, regulatory, and contractual findings into a clear view of asset condition, demonstrated capability, required capital, schedule, and execution risk.
Translate findings into recommendations for valuation assumptions, transaction structure, closing conditions, representations and warranties, indemnities, capital plans, and post-closing priorities.
Direct and challenge independent engineers, integrity specialists, hydraulic consultants, environmental consultants, and other technical advisors so their work addresses the relevant commercial and investment questions.
Prepare and present concise reports and investment materials for senior management, distinguishing confirmed facts, assumptions, sensitivities, unresolved issues, and recommended mitigations.

Cross Functional Collaboration

Partner with gas origination, engineering, environmental permitting, corporate strategy, business development, finance, legal, construction, operations, and asset-management teams.
Support commercial and legal teams in reviewing technical provisions of transportation, storage, interconnection, joint venture, acquisition, and transition-services agreements.
Maintain diligence procedures, operating benchmarks, lessons learned, and a qualified network of pipeline, integrity, hydraulic, and generation specialists.
Support asset onboarding and handoff through prioritized risk registers, capital plans, document-gap assessments, and clear ownership of open technical items.

Bachelor's degree in mechanical, chemical, civil, petroleum, electrical, or a closely related engineering discipline from an accredited institution.
Twelve to twenty years of progressively responsible experience with a major interstate or intrastate pipeline company, midstream operator, oil and gas exploration and production company, independent power producer, utility, original equipment manufacturer, or engineering advisory firm.
Deep technical experience in natural gas pipelines and system operations, including hydraulics, compression, integrity management, operating reliability, and applicable PHMSA requirements.
Experience evaluating pipeline projects or operating assets for acquisition, investment, expansion, commercial commitment, major capital approval, or independent engineering review.
Working knowledge of gas-fired power generation and the relationship among plant operating requirements, pipeline deliverability, transportation, storage, pressure, gas quality, and contingency supply.
Ability to interpret hydraulic studies, engineering reports, operating data, inspection records, drawings, permits, tariffs, contracts, cost estimates, schedules, maintenance records, and investment-model assumptions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting material risks and recommendations to senior executives and investment committees.
Ability to manage multiple time-sensitive workstreams and travel approximately 25% to 40%, including asset and project site visits.

Professional Engineer license, advanced engineering degree, or MBA.
Direct experience in pipeline operations, control-room management, compression engineering, integrity management, system planning, storage operations, or major-project development.
Experience with interstate pipeline tariffs and operating requirements, gas transportation and storage contracts, and joint venture or project-development agreements.
Experience evaluating simple-cycle or combined-cycle power plants, including assets supporting large industrial or data center loads.
Experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, representations and warranties diligence, lender or independent engineer reviews, and post-acquisition integration.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Director, Gas Infrastructure to add pipeline-specific technical depth to Hanwha Energy USA's growing natural gas infrastructure and generation initiatives. The Director will serve as the company's lead technical resource for the evaluation and advancement of pipeline transportation, storage, compression, interconnection, and other gas infrastructure opportunities. The role will also support technical due diligence for gas-fired generation and related infrastructure investments.

The Director will lead technical workstreams from early screening through due diligence, investment approval, contracting support, and project handoff. Responsibilities include assessing physical feasibility, system operations, integrity and reliability, capital requirements, schedule considerations, and execution risks, and translating those findings into actionable recommendations for development, investment, and operational decision-making. For gas-fired acquisitions and investments, the Director will focus on fuel supply infrastructure, pipeline connectivity, and related technical considerations while coordinating broader plant evaluations with engineering and external subject matter experts.

This role serves as the company's primary technical authority for natural gas transportation and infrastructure matters. The position is responsible for evaluating infrastructure opportunities, identifying technical risks and constraints, supporting strategic planning efforts, and providing technical expertise throughout the project lifecycle. The role works closely with commercial, engineering, environmental, regulatory, and operational teams to ensure infrastructure decisions are grounded in sound technical analysis and aligned with business objectives. Pipeline Infrastructure and System Operations

Assess pipeline hydraulics, pressure profiles, compression requirements, system bottlenecks, fuel use, redundancy, outage exposure, expansion capability, and practical gas deliverability under normal and peak conditions.
Review pipeline operating data, maintenance practices, control-room management, SCADA and telecommunications, cybersecurity interfaces, emergency response, operator qualification, and reliability risks.
Evaluate integrity-management programs, inline inspection and direct-assessment results, corrosion control, anomaly remediation, class location and high-consequence areas, maximum allowable operating pressure records, leak history, and remaining-life considerations.

Commercial Support

Test proposed capacity and deliverability against hydraulic studies, compressor availability, outage assumptions, receipt and delivery pressures, gas quality requirements, downstream constraints, tariff provisions, and operating requirements.
Review route, design basis, constructability, cost estimates, schedule, procurement strategy, commissioning plans, and cost-to-complete exposure for pipeline additions and expansions; provide inputs to the Environmental Permitting Manager for permit strategy and schedule.
Provide technical assumptions for commercial negotiations and investment models, including capacity, availability, fuel loss, operating cost, maintenance capital, expansion capital, schedule, and contingency.

Gas Asset Due Diligence

Support technical due diligence for acquisitions and investments involving simple-cycle and combined-cycle generation assets, with particular emphasis on fuel supply infrastructure, pipeline interfaces, pressure and gas-quality requirements, storage, firm transportation, and no-notice capability.

Integrate engineering, operational, environmental, regulatory, and contractual findings into a clear view of asset condition, demonstrated capability, required capital, schedule, and execution risk.
Translate findings into recommendations for valuation assumptions, transaction structure, closing conditions, representations and warranties, indemnities, capital plans, and post-closing priorities.
Direct and challenge independent engineers, integrity specialists, hydraulic consultants, environmental consultants, and other technical advisors so their work addresses the relevant commercial and investment questions.
Prepare and present concise reports and investment materials for senior management, distinguishing confirmed facts, assumptions, sensitivities, unresolved issues, and recommended mitigations.

Cross Functional Collaboration

Partner with gas origination, engineering, environmental permitting, corporate strategy, business development, finance, legal, construction, operations, and asset-management teams.
Support commercial and legal teams in reviewing technical provisions of transportation, storage, interconnection, joint venture, acquisition, and transition-services agreements.

Twelve to twenty years of progressively responsible experience with a major interstate or intrastate pipeline company, midstream operator, oil and gas exploration and production company, independent power producer, utility, original equipment manufacturer, or engineering advisory firm.
Deep technical experience in natural gas pipelines and system operations, including hydraulics, compression, integrity management, operating reliability, and applicable PHMSA requirements.
Experience evaluating pipeline projects or operating assets for acquisition, investment, expansion, commercial commitment, major capital approval, or independent engineering review.
Working knowledge of gas-fired power generation and the relationship among plant operating requirements, pipeline deliverability, transportation, storage, pressure, gas quality, and contingency supply.
Ability to interpret hydraulic studies, engineering reports, operating data, inspection records, drawings, permits, tariffs, contracts, cost estimates, schedules, maintenance records, and investment-model assumptions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting material risks and recommendations to senior executives and investment committees.
Ability to manage multiple time-sensitive workstreams and travel approximately 25% to 40%, including asset and project site visits.

Professional Engineer license, advanced engineering degree, or MBA.
Direct experience in pipeline operations, control-room management, compression engineering, integrity management, system planning, storage operations, or major-project development.
Experience with interstate pipeline tariffs and operating requirements, gas transportation and storage contracts, and joint venture or project-development agreements.
